summary.value: The Brakel is a Belgian chicken with a long history; records trace it back to the early 1400s in Flanders, a region that once reached from northern France into Belgium and Holland. It takes its name from a village northwest of Brussels. For centuries it was a common farm bird, and it was long lumped together with the Campine until the two were split in 1884. Both World Wars cut numbers badly, and by the 1960s it was almost gone. A rescue started in 1971 with just two hens, two roosters and a dozen eggs. Brakels come in silver or gold, with a solid colored neck and barred body feathers. Cocks weigh about 4.5 to 5.5 pounds and hens about 4 to 5 pounds. Hens lay around 180 to 200 large white eggs a year. The birds are active, strong fliers and keen foragers, best suited to free range.
